questions.cardText:
[Literature] What type of literary composition is the following? “An old silent pond/ A frog jumps into the pond/ Splash! Silence again.”
A. A haiku B. A ballad C. An ode
Answer: A. Haiku is a form of poetry that originated in Japan, and its traditional subjects include nature, the seasons, and the fleeting nature of existence. A haiku traditionally consists of three lines with a 5-7-5 syllable structure. This Haiku was composed by Matsuo Bashō in the 1600s.
questions.de: Welche japanische Gedichtform ist Matsuo Bashōs „Ein alter stiller Teich / Ein Frosch springt in den Teich / Platsch! Wieder Stille“?
questions.en: What form of Japanese poem is Matsuo Bashō's "An old silent pond / A frog jumps into the pond / Splash! Silence again"?

timeline.labelEn: Matsuo Bashō composes his "old pond" frog haiku
timeline.labelDe: Matsuo Bashō verfasst sein Frosch-Haiku vom „alten Teich“

questions.notes: In Bashō's day it was a hokku; the name haiku came from Masaoka Shiki in the late 19th century. The 5-7-5 count is of Japanese morae (on), not English syllables — the card's translation doesn't fit it.

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] What is a “supernova”?
A. A newly formed star
B. The explosion of a star
C. The collision between two black holes
Answer: B. A supernova can briefly outshine an entire galaxy and radiate more energy than our sun will in its entire lifetime. The explosion expels much of a star’s material into space.
questions.de: Wie heißt die gewaltige Explosion eines Sterns, die kurzzeitig eine ganze Galaxie überstrahlen kann?
questions.en: What is the name for the powerful explosion of a star that can briefly outshine an entire galaxy?

timeline.labelEn: Walter Baade and Fritz Zwicky begin using the word "supernova" in lectures
timeline.labelDe: Walter Baade und Fritz Zwicky verwenden das Wort „Supernova“ erstmals in Vorlesungen
